newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Transport ministers urge EU to act on air safety.
newsitem.headline: Transport ministers urge EU to act on air safety.

text.p: European Union transport ministers on Saturday urged the European Commission to push ahead with institutionalising air transport safety during the final day of an informal transport council in Amsterdam.

"We have only just begun to scratch at the surface of (air safety)... The JAA (Joint Aviation Authority) remains a weak sibling of its American counterpart. Decision-making must be streamlined," said Dutch transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma.
The European Commission has proposed the establishment of a European Aviation Safety Authority to formalise the functions performed by the JAA.
"We all have very high safety standards, but the aim is to set up a kind of European FAA (the U.S.'s Federal Aviation Authority)," said Jorritsma.
Ministers also tackled the related issue of air traffic management, echoing the Commission's view that the EU cannot operate as an island within Europe.
"We reached a conclusion that a joint approach even beyond the frontiers of the Union is called for," said Jorritsma.
Both air traffic management and air safety are seen as vital to the steady opening of the skies over Europe.
On both issues, Jorritsma said she expected progress from the Commission during the six-month Dutch presidency, possibly as early as the formal EU transport council in March.
"We agreed that the Commission will deliver serious proposals under the Netherlands' presidency and we will have a serious debate in March and June."
European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock agreed that swift progress was possible.
"We can reach a conclusive set of decisions well within the time of the Dutch presidency," he said.

Kinnock added that, within a couple of weeks, the Commission will adopt a proposal on "ramp checks", to ensure planes from third countries meet European safety criteria. However, he said it was not the Commission's intention to draw up a blacklist of unsafe countries.
